extracted.intended_audience: applicants seeking registration to practice before the USPTO; attorneys/agents filing petitions under 37 C.F.R. §11.2(d); practitioners interacting with OED
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for petitions asking the USPTO Director to review an OED Director's final decision on applications for registration to practice before the USPTO (including waiver requests of the registration examination and moral-character determinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good moral character and reputation required for registration (37 C.F.R. § 11.7(a)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director requires agents, attorneys, or other persons to show that they are of good moral character and reputation prior to registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director investigates moral character and reputation as part of acting on applications for registration. An applicant must satisfactorily establish that he/she presently possesses the good moral character and reputation required to represent applicants before the USPTO; failure to do so is a ground for denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant bears burden of proof to establish moral character
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must meet the burden of establishing that he presently possesses good moral character and reputation as required by 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(a)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not meet this burden, the OED Director may deny registration. The decision shows OED will require a preponderance of evidence (practical standard) to conclude the applicant satisfies the moral-character requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of the registration examination (37 C.F.R. § 11.7(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking registration by waiver of the registration examination must demonstrate entitlement to that waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED may issue a Show Cause Requirement if the applicant has not shown the examination should be waived. Failure to demonstrate eligibility for waiver is a proper ground for disapproval of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of petition for review (37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for review of the OED Director's final decision must be filed with the OED Director within sixty days of the mailing date of the final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions not filed within sixty days 'will be dismissed as untimely.' The controlling date is the mailing date of the final decision, not the date of receipt. The petition must also be accompanied by payment of the appropriate fee required under 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(5)(ii). If a petition is untimely, the USPTO Director will dismiss it and decline to consider the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver/suspension of rules only in extraordinary situations (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may seek suspension of any requirement of the rules in an 'extraordinary situation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a suspension requires a compelling showing of extraordinary circumstances. Ordinary mistakes about dates or unsupported assertions are insufficient to justify waiving the timely-filing requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural consequence: merits not considered if procedural requirements unmet
rubrics_metrics.description: If procedural requirements (such as timely filing) are not met, the USPTO Director will decline to consider the substantive merits of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision explicitly states the Office will not reach the merits when a petition is untimely; dismissal on procedural grounds forecloses substantive review unless a valid rule suspension is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's authority and processes (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.2(b)(2)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director receives and acts on applications for registration, including conducting investigations into moral character and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual dissatisfied with the OED Director's final decision may petition the USPTO Director for review under § 11.2(d), subject to the procedural requirements (filing deadline, fee). The OED Director also issues Show Cause Requirements when grounds for disapproval exist.
